name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,594

clue.text: Award most of money before rift

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it bar its final letter
before places the shortened money ahead of the award in the answer

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, here losing its last letter
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: Someone is handed an honour and a cash prize before a quarrel breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: The award comes first in the clue but last in the answer. The Companion of Honour is an order conferred by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a break or gap, including a split in a relationship or a broken wall.

clue.text: Treacherous revolutionary initially escaping capture in retreat

indicators.note: the word's first letter escapes, so it is dropped from the front
something in retreat goes back, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a Trot, short for Trotskyist, minus its opening letter
to net something is to capture it

explanation.surface: A rebel slips out of custody just as the army falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten in the sense of corrupt and morally bad can describe a traitorous, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Soldier quick to learn about unserviceable gear

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
an apt pupil picks things up quickly
U/S is the abbreviation for unserviceable

explanation.surface: A bright recruit is set to work on some broken army equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick to learn' reads as praise for the soldier, but it is a separate piece that wraps round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment or tackle assembled for a particular purpose, which is what gear means.

clue.text: Greeting round of applause with a wave

blocks.note: to give someone a big hand is to applaud them
a shake is a waving or wagging movement

explanation.surface: A performer is welcomed by clapping and a wave from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and pumping hands is a customary way people say hello on meeting.

clue.text: Fond of an upset occasionally

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone is only sometimes keen on a person who gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Done intermittently, now and then rather than continuously, so at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Not in time to protect king from violent injury

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the outer words go round the king

blocks.note: the opposite of in
an age is a period of time
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A bodyguard arrives too late to shield the monarch from an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT and AGE together surround R.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is an act of great violence or cruelty, an atrocity or grievous wrong.

clue.text: Biting Bill to get free

blocks.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
to get rid of is to free oneself of

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill bites his way out of captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name but is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid smell or remark is pungent and sharp, stinging like something biting.

clue.text: Doctor involved in study of genius

indicators.note: something involved in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a den is a private study or room
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A physician takes part in research into brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon at something is a prodigy or wizard, someone with outstanding skill or talent.

clue.text: Silly to pay Heather

blocks.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: It seems foolish that Heather should be the one paying.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Footling means trivial and pointless, an old-fashioned word for foolish or petty.

clue.text: Inept sot struggling to go faster

indicators.note: struggling suggests flailing about, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A clumsy drunk has trouble picking up the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom telling someone to hurry, from pressing the accelerator pedal.

clue.text: Type of film showing end of panic after months in space

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
after places the panic letter following the month
in puts these letters inside the space word

blocks.note: m is the abbreviation for month or months
the last letter of panic
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A film about panic breaking out after months adrift in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests science fiction; 'space' is simply room.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom is a romantic comedy, a familiar genre of cinema.

clue.text: Left-leaning plot against Republican is in ruins

indicators.note: leaning to the left in an across clue means running backwards, right to left
against means next to, so the following pieces are placed alongside

blocks.note: a garden plot or flower bed
R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written

explanation.surface: A left-wing conspiracy against a Republican lies in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in' is the joining phrase, with 'is' used twice: once as letters and once as link. 'Left-leaning plot' reads as political scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something destroyed, which is what ruins are.

clue.text: Somewhat powerless to embrace retreat in an enthusiastic manner

indicators.note: powerless means without P, the abbreviation for power
to embrace is to hold round, so these letters go around the next

blocks.note: partly means somewhat, here without its P
a den is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: A rather weak figure eagerly hugs a quiet hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something ardently means with passion and zeal, so with keen fervour.

clue.text: Old English flower

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A traditional English bloom, perhaps a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower in crosswords is often something that flows, a river: the Exe runs through Devon to Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river in south-west England, and a river is a thing that flows.

clue.text: Detect hint of micronutrient

blocks.note: to trace something is to find or detect it
an element of something is a small amount or touch of it

explanation.surface: Tests pick up a faint sign of an essential mineral in the diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trace elements such as zinc or iodine are chemicals the body requires only in tiny quantities.

clue.text: Become discouraged as Larwood would if wicketless

definitions.note: a cryptic second definition describing the letters of a name, not a meaning

blocks.note: first meaning: to lose courage or hope
second reading: the name Larwood without W, the abbreviation for wicket, loses its central letter

explanation.walkthrough: Harold Larwood was an England fast bowler, famous for the 1932-33 Bodyline series; a bowler without wickets might lose heart. But W is also the middle letter of LARWOOD, so dropping it removes the name's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for growing dispirited and losing confidence or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Largely avoid imparting a feeling of doubt

indicators.note: largely means mostly, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to miss is to avoid, cut short here
imparting something is giving it

explanation.surface: Someone mostly holds back from passing on their reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a qualm or apprehension, a sense that something may be wrong.

clue.text: Changed planes at Nice

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the following letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A traveller switched flights at Nice airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city on the Riviera, capitalised as the first word of the place; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and nice are everyday synonyms for agreeable or enjoyable.

clue.text: Starts with places producing protective coverings

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of material, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin with locations that yield something protective.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster casts are rigid moulds set around broken limbs to shield and immobilise them while healing.

clue.text: Essential to list each kind of shrub

indicators.note: essential to means forming the inner part, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A gardener's advice that every variety of bush must be listed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea plant, Camellia sinensis, is an evergreen bush whose leaves are dried for brewing.

clue.text: Last of victims well hidden by murderer in watertight chamber

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
something hidden by another is concealed inside it

blocks.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
the final letter of victims
so and well both open a remark: 'well, what now?'

explanation.surface: A killer hides the final body down a well inside a sealed vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's well is a hole in the ground; it is really the interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is a sealed, water-excluding structure used for underwater construction work such as bridge foundations.

clue.text: Slightly alter poster before fair

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, can be a poster
fair and just both mean impartial

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks a placard advertising a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to make a small modification or correction to something.

clue.text: Vital energy associated with girl band for instance

definitions.note: mariachi is a kind of band, so the definition is by example

blocks.note: a girl's name
chi is the life force in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: An energetic young woman joins a girl band.
explanation.walkthrough: The vital energy comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi is a style of Mexican folk music played by a small group of strolling musicians.

clue.text: Form of Arabic art originally covered by Irish TV show

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter counts
something covered by others is enclosed within them

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
the first letter of art
QI is a British TV quiz show hosted first by Stephen Fry

explanation.surface: Arabic calligraphy appears on an Irish television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqi Arabic is the regional dialect of the language spoken in Iraq.

clue.text: Caught with order for crystal-meth

blocks.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a rank is an order or grade; with simply joins it on

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is arrested while placing an order for methamphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: Crank is street slang for methamphetamine, especially in its crystalline form.

clue.text: Henry to broadcast with Rob and Bob possibly

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
to air a programme is to broadcast it
to do someone is slang for to cheat or rob them

explanation.surface: Henry is going on air alongside two men named Rob and Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob and Bob look like a pair of presenters; one is a verb and the other a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short, straight haircut, one example of a styled arrangement of hair.

clue.text: Tomorrow's article filled with spiritual nourishment? Just the opposite

indicators.note: filled with puts one thing inside another
this reverses the roles just stated, so the outer and inner words swap

blocks.note: mana is spiritual power or authority, from Polynesian belief
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article for the morrow, full of food for the soul.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken straight, the article would hold the nourishment; 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles, so the nourishment holds the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, borrowed into English for an indefinite later time.

clue.text: Roomy and deceptively attractive with area for a bit of exercise

indicators.note: with one thing in place of another means swap them

blocks.note: specious means superficially plausible but actually wrong
A is the abbreviation for area
the first letter of exercise, the bit taken out

explanation.surface: A spacious gym that looks inviting and has room for a quick workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of SPECIOUS becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means having ample space, so roomy is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Affected by onset of nerves after hoax in the London area

indicators.note: in puts the hoax inside the London area
the onset of something is its beginning, so the first letter
after places the nerves letter at the end

blocks.note: SE is the postal district for south-east London
a trick or prank
the first letter of nerves

explanation.surface: Someone in London is shaken by a prank that sets their nerves jangling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken means badly afflicted, as by grief or illness, so seriously troubled.

clue.text: Item of clothing hard to obtain close to Christmas

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

blocks.note: money is tight when it is scarce
the final letter of Christmas

explanation.surface: A popular gift is sold out as Christmas nears.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting garment of stretchy fabric covering the legs and lower body.
